We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

The contributions you will make:
The Engineering Intern is a temporary developmental role designed to provide students with practical experience building and operating modern digital solutions while developing the technical, professional, and business capabilities needed for a successful software engineering career. Working within a cross-functional product team and with close guidance from experienced engineers, this role contributes to well-defined software design, development, testing, automation, deployment, support, and improvement activities while learning how engineering work connects to product objectives, client needs, and business value. The Engineering Intern develops learning agility by actively seeking coaching, rapidly applying feedback and new knowledge, and responsibly exploring cloud-native, DevSecOps, automation, observability, AI-enabled tools and practices, Agentic AI patterns, and AI agents.
A typical day:
Own Engineering Delivery by completing well-defined engineering assignments under guidance, with attention to quality, security, reliability, maintainability, supportability, testing, documentation, and established engineering standards.
Develop Technical Foundations and Learning Agility by applying software engineering fundamentals while learning the team's technologies, domain concepts, and modern cloud-native, DevSecOps, automated testing, CI/CD, observability, and delivery practices.
Demonstrates curiosity, actively seeks coaching, experiments responsibly within established guardrails, and rapidly applies feedback and new knowledge.
Uses AI-enabled engineering tools and practices, Agentic AI patterns, and AI agents with appropriate supervision to accelerate learning and improve productivity and quality while validating results, protecting sensitive information, and maintaining human accountability.
Connect Engineering to Business Outcomes by developing an understanding of product goals, client needs, business priorities, and how assigned engineering work contributes to team objectives and meaningful business value. Begins building a trusted, value-added partner mindset by listening to comprehend, asking thoughtful questions, offering relevant observations, and reliably following through on commitments.
Strengthen Team Effectiveness by actively participating in Agile ceremonies, technical discussions, code reviews, testing, documentation, operational support, root-cause learning, and continuous improvement.
Demonstrates resilience by adapting to feedback and changing priorities, learning from mistakes and setbacks, and persisting through routine technical challenges.
Collaborate Across Teams by building productive and trusted working relationships with engineers, quality engineers, product managers, architects, platform engineers, UX designers, and business partners.
Build Personal Capability by actively seeking coaching, reflecting on experiences, rapidly applying feedback and new knowledge, sharing learning, and demonstrating accountability for growth.
Contributes to an inclusive, positive, and engaging environment where team members take the work seriously, enjoy working together, and recognize progress and success while preparing for potential progression into an Associate Engineer role.
The skills and experience we prefer you have:
Currently pursuing a Bachelor or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical discipline.
Completion of coursework in programming, software engineering fundamentals, algorithms, data structures, or comparable technical subjects.
Experience developing software through academic coursework, personal projects, hackathons, research, open-source contributions, or comparable learning experiences.
Demonstrated learning agility through curiosity, active feedback seeking, rapid application of new technical concepts, and adaptation of approaches to solve problems.
Experience with one or more modern programming languages or development frameworks.
Exposure to cloud-native application development concepts and one or more cloud platforms.
Familiarity with Git-based source control and Agile software development.
Exposure to automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, DevSecOps, or observability practices.
Ability to develop clean, maintainable, and well-tested software while working under appropriate guidance and established engineering practices.
Ability to analyze routine technical problems, ask effective questions, and apply foundational engineering principles to identify solutions.
Ability to responsibly use AI-enabled engineering tools and practices, Agentic AI patterns, and AI agents with appropriate supervision while applying critical thinking, validating outputs, protecting sensitive information, maintaining human accountability, and following engineering standards.
Ability to demonstrate learning agility by actively seeking and applying feedback, rapidly acquiring new knowledge, experimenting within appropriate guardrails, reflecting on outcomes, and continuously improving technical and professional capabilities.
Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders; listens to comprehend, asks thoughtful questions, builds trust through reliable follow-through, and begins contributing value-added observations or ideas.
Ability to collaborate within cross-functional product teams, incorporate feedback and diverse perspectives, and contribute to an inclusive, positive, and engaging team environment.
Ability to organize assigned work, adapt to changing priorities, and persist through routine ambiguity, mistakes, setbacks, and technical challenges.
Understanding of secure software development fundamentals, quality engineering principles, and the responsibility to protect confidential information and client data.

This internship is designed for a student who wants to explore talent acquisition as a potential career and is curious about how people, business, technology, research, and data come together to make recruiting effective.
About the Internship
Dev Technology Group, Inc. is seeking a talented rising Junior or Senior for our Summer Internship Program. The intern will be based out of our headquarters in Reston, Virginia, and must be able to commute to the office a minimum of two days each week. We do not provide summer internship housing.
The Talent Team Intern will gain hands-on experience in talent acquisition while learning how recruiting supports Dev Technology's business, projects, customers, and growth. The intern will learn the fundamentals of identifying and sourcing talent, reviewing candidate qualifications, maintaining accurate recruiting data, and using research and basic analysis to support recruiting decisions.
Throughout the summer, the intern will work with Talent Team members, observe recruiter and hiring-manager strategy discussions, and gain exposure to corporate operations, project teams, business development, and federal government contracting. The goal is not for the intern to become an independent recruiter in 10 weeks, but to build a strong foundation and demonstrate curiosity, judgment, accuracy, and an interest in developing as a recruiting professional.
As part of the broader Summer Intern Program, the intern will also learn about technology trends, professional work environments, and government contracting. Interns collaborate with fellow summer interns on a technically focused project and present the group's results to the executive team at the end of the program.
What You'll Be Doing
Assist recruiters with sourcing candidates for technical and corporate positions using job boards, professional networks, the Dev Talent Network, and other research tools.
Learn basic sourcing and search techniques and how to identify potential candidates based on the skills and experience required for a position.
Research available market talent and help build talent pipelines for difficult-to-fill and frequently needed roles.
Review resumes and candidate profiles and help develop pre-screening questions to assess qualifications for specific roles.
Attend selected corporate-level meetings and learning sessions to gain exposure to areas such as business development, finance, project management, and federal contracting.
Assist with college recruiting activities and future summer internship planning.
Explore practical ways AI and other technology can support candidate research, sourcing, data analysis, and recruiting productivity.
Observe recruiter and hiring-manager strategy meetings to learn how business and project needs translate into recruiting requirements.
Maintain accurate and complete candidate records in the applicant tracking system (ATS), with a strong emphasis on data quality and attention to detail.
Use Excel, the ATS, and other tools to organize recruiting information, pull basic reports, and help identify useful trends or insights.
Assist with creating job descriptions and posting openings on relevant platforms and within the ATS.
Communicate with candidates and help support a positive candidate experience throughout the recruiting process.
Assist with talent-network communications, employee referrals, Dev Technology alumni outreach, and candidate-engagement campaigns.
Assist with contingent recruiting for proposals, including candidate research and resume formatting as needed.
Collaborate with Talent Team members on special projects and initiatives as needed.

How to look beyond keywords and begin assessing whether a candidate's experience aligns with a role.
How recruiters research and identify talent using multiple sources and search approaches.
Why understanding the business, customer, project, and technology matters when recruiting.
How accurate ATS and talent-database information supports better recruiting decisions.
How Excel, reporting, research, and basic analysis can make talent acquisition more effective.
How recruiters build candidate relationships and talent pipelines over time.
How a government contracting company connects talent acquisition to current projects, proposals, and future growth.
By the end of the internship, a successful intern should be able to review a recruiting requirement, conduct basic candidate research, identify several potentially relevant candidates, explain the reasoning behind those selections, and accurately document the work in the appropriate recruiting systems. Just as important, the intern should leave with a better understanding of Dev Technology's business and whether talent acquisition is a career they want to continue developing after college.

Curiosity about how a company operates and how customers, projects, technology, and business needs influence hiring.
Interest in using data, technology, databases, and research to make recruiting more effective.
Strong attention to detail and an appreciation for accurate, well-maintained information.

Ability to be proactive, dependable, ask thoughtful questions, accept feedback, and follow tasks through to completion.
Strong organizational and time-management skills in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills and an interest in developing candidate relationship and interviewing skills.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.
A mindset that demonstrates flexibility, resilience, adaptability, and a desire to learn.

About the Team
The DoorDash Research Fellowship is a 3-month program (extendable to 6 months) looking for Summer and Fall 2026 cohorts, for researchers and engineers who want to work on the hardest applied ML and AI problems in local commerce. Fellows are given the resources, autonomy, and access to real-world operational data needed to pursue ambitious research directions — with the goal of producing work that influences both the field and how DoorDash operates at scale.
This program is modeled on the best external research fellowships: fellows are treated as independent researchers, not as junior employees on a product team. You pick the problem (within a set of priority areas), you own the direction, and you publish or ship the outcome.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will receive…
Dedicated compute allocation sized to the research agenda — GPU clusters for training and inference budgets for experimentation
Full access to DoorDash's research infrastructure — our internal RL stack, training and evaluation pipelines, RL environments built on real operational systems, agent evaluation harnesses, and the tooling our own research teams use day-to-day. Fellows are first-class users, not sandboxed visitors.
Access to DoorDash operational data — real-world datasets spanning logistics, merchant operations, consumer behavior, and marketplace dynamics, under appropriate data governance
Research mentorship from senior researchers and engineering leaders at DoorDash, plus a named research sponsor for each fellow who meets with you weekly and is accountable for unblocking your work
Speaker series featuring leading researchers and practitioners from academia and industry — faculty from top ML programs, research leads from frontier AI labs, and senior operators from across tech. Fellows get dedicated 1:1 time with speakers when possible.
A cohort of fellows working alongside you — a small, tight-knit group of researchers tackling different problems but sharing ideas, drafts, and reading groups. The community extends to DoorDash research alumni and the broader fellowship network.
Publication support — fellows are encouraged to publish at top venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, KDD, etc.) and DoorDash will support the legal and review process
Relocation support, housing stipend, and competitive pay
Structure
Kickoff (2 weeks, in-person in SF): Onboarding, scoping the research agenda with your sponsor, meeting teams across Research, ML Platform, and relevant product orgs
Core research period (~10 weeks, hybrid from SF DoorDash office): Focused research work with regular check-ins, internal talks, and working sessions. Extension to 6 months decided at the midpoint based on research progress and mutual fit.
Closeout: Final write-up, internal presentation, and publication or productionization path
Priority Research Areas
Fellows are welcome to propose their own direction, but we are particularly interested in work across:
Reinforcement learning environments for real-world operations — building high-fidelity simulators and training environments from operational data, including the tradeoffs between real-data fidelity and synthetic generalization
Agentic systems for logistics and local commerce — long-horizon planning, tool use, and evaluation methodologies for agents operating in physical-world marketplaces
Foundation models for marketplace dynamics — forecasting, pricing, matching, and personalization at marketplace scale
Evaluation and measurement — new benchmarks and evaluation methods for ML systems deployed in messy, real-world operational settings
Multimodal understanding — vision, speech, and language applied to merchant catalogs, operations, and consumer interfaces
We’re excited about you because…
You’re a researcher with a strong track record — PhD candidates (rising 4th year or beyond), recent PhDs, or independent researchers with published work at top ML venues or equivalent demonstrated output
You’re an engineer with deep research instincts who have shipped ambitious ML or systems work and want dedicated time to pursue a research direction
You can operate independently — set a research agenda, scope it, and execute without heavy supervision
You have strong written and verbal communication; comfort presenting work to mixed research and engineering audiences
We are not looking for specific years of experience or specific degrees. Exceptional candidates from non-traditional backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.
Compensation
The fellowship is 12 weeks long with potential opportunity for extension. The fellow’s starting pay will fall within the monthly pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including education, work location, and market conditions.
Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base pay, fellows are eligible for both a housing stipend and relocation stipend. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer our fellows a wellness reimbursement benefit, access to an employee assistance program, in-office lunch credits and more!
Base Pay (Monthly)
$8,500—$16,000 USD

As a Quantitative Trading Analyst Intern, you will gain exposure to the dynamic worlds of trading and technology in order to learn what it takes to become a successful and sustainable trader. You will work on a small team to combine the disciplines of technology, research and risk management to identify optimal trading and investment strategies within the regulatory framework through a series of project based assignments. Collaborate with senior traders, technologists and quantitative researchers by developing and improving trading strategies by working directly on the trading desk
Identify and research in the development of cutting-edge market research projects using powerful analytic tools
Market research projects vary from macroeconomic data curation and analysis to application of machine learning techniques to market tick data for automated trading
Be given immediate responsibility through assignments like position tracking, calculating risk, and analyzing vital theoretical values
What you bring to the team…
Are pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s or PhD in mathematics, economics, physics, statistics, computer science or any engineering related field and have an expected graduation date between December 2027 and June 2028
Advanced quantitative, analytical and problem-solving skills and the ability to deploy those skills under time-sensitive situations
Proficient programming in Python

A passion for the financial markets and a deep curiosity to explore new methodologies
Strong communication skills to advocate your ideas in a clear and concise manner to the group

Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Machine Learning, AI, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field.

Exposure to real-world projects involving data analysis, predictive modeling, or automation.
Interest in the legal technology domain or experience working with enterprise-grade systems.

Impactful Work: Be part of a team that’s at the forefront of AI innovation.

Dynamic Culture: Join a group of passionate, driven individuals who are committed to making a difference.

Faraday Future is a California-based technology company focused on the design, engineering, and development of intelligent, connected electric vehicles and related artificial intelligence–enabled technologies.

Join us in shaping the future of intelligent transportation and technology by creating something new, something connected, and something with a true global impact.
Your Role:
The Product Marketing Intern will support product marketing initiatives for Faraday Future's robotics-related business and product programs. This role will help translate robotics product features, use cases, and technical capabilities into clear, compelling marketing messages, product selling points, and creative campaign ideas. This role is based in El Segundo, CA.
The intern will work closely with product, marketing, design, and business teams to support the June launch event and follow-up go-to-market activities.
Key Responsibilities:
Product Marketing Support:
Assist in summarizing robotics product features, use cases, user benefits, and key selling points for marketing and launch communication.
Market & Competitor Research:
Conduct basic research on robotics, AI, intelligent mobility, and consumer technology trends. Help analyze competitor products, marketing messages, and campaign ideas.
Messaging & Creative Ideation:
Support the development of product marketing messages, campaign angles, social media themes, and creative concepts based on product positioning and user scenarios.
AI-Enabled Marketing Support:
Use mainstream Gen AI image and video tools to support marketing ideation, visual exploration, video concepts, and creative development.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
Work with product, marketing, and design teams to collect product information, clarify product value, and ensure marketing messages are accurate and aligned with business goals.
Basic Qualifications:
Education:
Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, Product Marketing, Media, Advertising, or a related field is preferred.
AI Tool Familiarity:
Familiar with mainstream Gen AI image and video tools, such as Grok, Midjourney, Sora, Seedance, Runway, Kling, Veo, or similar platforms.
Passion & Interest:
Strong interest in robotics, AI, intelligent mobility, EVs, consumer technology, and product marketing.
Communication Skills:
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to turn product information into clear and compelling marketing language.
Creative Thinking:
Strong creative sense and ability to develop product storytelling ideas, campaign concepts, and social media communication angles.
Ownership:
Proactive, detail-oriented, organized, and able to take initiative and follow through on assigned tasks in a fast-paced environment.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience or coursework related to product marketing, marketing communications, digital marketing, robotics, AI, EVs, or consumer technology.
Familiarity with social media platforms, digital marketing trends, and short-form video formats.
Experience using creative tools such as Canva, CapCut, Adobe Creative Suite, Figma, or similar platforms is a plus.
Bilingual English and Chinese capability is preferred.

($18/HR-$21/HR)

Healthcare + dental + vision benefits (Free for you/discounted for family)

Casual dress code + relaxed work environment
Culturally diverse, progressive atmosphere

As an Accounting Intern, you will support the day-to-day accounting operations of a public-company finance team — working with real transactions, reconciliations, month-end close, and supporting schedules — with additional focus on using AI to automate the repetitive parts of accounting. Technical Skills: Comfortable learning and working in financial systems (e.g., accounting / ERP software) and with large, detailed sets of transaction data.

AI tools: Comfort with AI tools and interest in AI-assisted automation (e.g., prompting AI to help with scripts or basic workflow automation) — you don’t need to be an engineer, but curiosity about automating manual accounting work goes a long way.

Job Description: Robotics Data Operator Intern
Category: Robotics / AI Data Operator
Location: LA, US
As the Intern of the Robotics Data Factory, you will be responsible for collecting high-fidelity human behavior and robot teleoperation data. This data is essential for training the next generation of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, helping robots learn to perceive and interact with the physical world by capturing real-world human interactions and precision robotic movements.
Key Responsibilities
Egocentric Data Collection: Wear designated head-mounted recording devices (e.g., smartphone rigs, GoPro, or head-mounted VR kits) to capture daily or industrial tasks from a first-person perspective in diverse environments (home, retail, or manufacturing).
VR Teleoperation: Operate robotic systems via VR interfaces to perform complex manipulation tasks. Ensure high-quality capture of multi-modal data, including joint states, torques, and gripper status, while maintaining low-latency execution.
Technical Specification Compliance: Maintain strict recording standards (1080p, 30FPS, horizontal orientation, FOV >130°). Ensure accurate extraction of camera intrinsic parameters and time-synchronization across all sensors.
Quality Assurance & Pre-processing: Conduct initial self-inspections to filter out clips with excessive shaking, occlusions, or focus failures. Ensure data is correctly formatted (e.g., MCAP, HDF5) and uploaded according to protocol.

Experience: 0–1 years of experience. Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
Extreme Attention to Detail: Ability to strictly follow complex technical guidelines regarding framing, motion rhythm, and lighting environments.
Technical Proficiency: Comfortable using smartphones, VR hardware (Meta Quest/HTC Vive), and various digital accessories. Basic understanding of video recording parameters and calibration.
Action Consistency: Ability to perform tasks naturally while maintaining the specific "robotic-friendly" pacing required for imitation learning.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience in Python, Linux command line.
Familiarity with ROS2, LeRobot, or AI data labeling workflows.
Strong interest in Embodied AI and robotics.

Glove Policy: Preference for bare hands; if necessary, only approved thin/transparent medical gloves are allowed. No thick or dark-colored gloves that obscure finger articulation.
Safety & Privacy: Must follow all site-specific safety protocols and strictly avoid capturing any Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or sensitive/prohibited scenarios.

What you’ll be part of
Garner is on a mission to transform the U.S. healthcare system — and we’re the only proven player doing exactly that. We partner with employers to redesign how healthcare works: applying 550+ proprietary clinical metrics across 80+ specialties to a dataset of 320M+ patients to identify the best-performing doctors, then using compelling incentives to steer members to the care that helps them get healthier, faster.
The result is a rare “win win” — better care and lower costs for both members and employers. In just five years, our work has helped over 2.5 million people access higher-quality care and saved $1B in healthcare costs. We recently raised our Series E and have doubled five years running. If you've ever wanted your work to solve a problem that touches every person in this country, this is the opportunity to do exactly that. You'd be joining a team fundamentally reimagining healthcare in the U.S. — and using AI to scale that impact further and faster than anyone else can.

We are seeking exceptional Software Engineering Interns for our 10-week summer program in New York City. As a core member of our engineering team, you'll build and launch features that directly impact real people — helping our members find top doctors and manage medical claims with ease.
You'll work alongside a passionate, multidisciplinary team of engineers, designers, and product managers, taking ownership of meaningful problems in a fast-paced, agile environment. This is hands-on experience building the systems that power our mission: transforming the healthcare economy to deliver high-quality, affordable care for all.
Select interns will be offered full-time roles upon successful completion of the program.
What you will do
Use AI to build, optimize, and maintain software systems
Collaborate across disciplines to understand our domain and iterate on projects
Participate in code reviews, sharing your insights and learning from others
Engage in problem solving sessions with senior engineers and team leads where your unique perspective will be valued
Deliver a capstone project presentation to engineering leaders and business stakeholders, demonstrating your work and impact
What we're looking for
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science or related STEM field (expected graduation Fall 2027–Spring 2028)
Solid CS fundamentals with exposure to front-end (JavaScript, React) or back-end (Python, Node.js) technologies; familiarity with databases or cloud platforms (AWS, Docker) is a plus
Exposure to or interest in building with AI coding agents (we use Claude Code) is a plus
Strong problem-solver who enjoys breaking down challenges and finding elegant solutions
Self-starter who takes ownership of their work and is motivated by real-world impact
Clear communicator who can discuss technical ideas with both technical and non-technical audiences, and takes feedback well
Excited by fast-paced environments and eager to stretch their skills
A desire to do work that matters: and to be held to a high standard while doing it. You're energized by a mission with measurable outcomes, not just good intentions. You engage with AI tools as part of how you do your best work, and hold yourself accountable to outcomes that matter beyond your team’s metrics

You’ll work on problems that matter, at a company working to change healthcare at scale. You’ll work at the intersection of AI and systemic healthcare reform, where the problems we solve are as interesting and compelling as the mission.
At Garner, you’ll take on real, ambitious problems with real ownership and autonomy, alongside exceptional, principles-based people who genuinely want you to win. It’s demanding by design. You’ll be challenged to stretch beyond what you thought possible and receive consistent coaching to help you grow and do the best work of your career. Claude Code, Kubernetes, AWS, Airflow, dlt, dbt, Python, TypeScript, React, Go

Gelber Group -- Passion for Trading. Powered by Technology.
Headquartered in Chicago with offices across the United States and Europe, Gelber has set the bar as one of the industry’s innovative and enduring proprietary trading firms for more than 40 years. Our collaborative and entrepreneurial culture empowers each member of our team to have a meaningful impact from the start. We pride ourselves on a flat organizational structure and focus on meritocracy. If you flourish in a fast-paced environment, have a strong work ethic, and a competitive attitude, Gelber is right for you.
As a Discretionary Trading Intern at Gelber Group, you will begin your 10-week internship with an education portion covering basics of liquid capital markets, the various ways in which Gelber engages these markets, and the tools and technology that link us to the markets. Once you have a grasp of these concepts, you will be assigned directly to a discretionary trading desk.
This internship will begin in June 2027 and last until the first week of August 2027. We are considering recent graduates or candidates that are graduating in 2027 or 2028.
The approximate hourly rate for this position in Chicago, IL is $35/hr. This is a temporary role and is not eligible for employee benefits.
Position Overview
We are seeking highly motivated individuals to participate in a summer program in which they will learn and practice the development and execution of a rates-first macro trading process. Our primary goal in the internship is to evaluate candidates for full-time employment. As a result, our interests are best served by teaching you the necessary skills to demonstrate your talent and potential.
What You’ll Do
Experience hands-on learning and sit on a trading desk with full-time traders
Gain a thorough understanding of the financial markets through a robust program that will be intensive, challenging, and fun
The classroom portion will be tailored to the topic areas that are useful for beginning to build a discretionary macro process
Topics may include a basic understanding of each asset class, macroeconomic fundamentals, technical analysis, and risk management
Develop a deep understanding of how macro traders engage with the market
Pitch weekly trade ideas and receive in-depth feedback on quality and execution
Potential for ideas to be turned into live risk taking
Experience a multi-week simulated trading experience
Send out daily and weekly reflections as you begin to build your own trading process
Build the foundation of a macro trading process
Goals
Gain hands on experience interacting with the market from a macro perspective
Determine if this is the career you want to pursue
Qualifications
Rising junior or senior in an undergraduate program, or recent graduate
Interest in financial markets is a must, but prior experience or knowledge is not required
Demonstrated interest in economics or a related field, via classwork or extracurricular activities
Curiosity, self-motivation, strong communication skills, and the ability to collaborate with others in a competitive environment
Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to learn, understand, and apply new concepts
Superior analytical skills with a proven strong mathematical aptitude

Brand new office in the heart of Chicago’s River North neighborhood, attached to the Merchandise Mart and “El” stop, and a short walk from both Ogilvie and Union Train Stations
Comprehensive 10-week program, running from June to August 2027

General Matter enriches uranium.

In the process, we are restoring America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel to power AI, advanced manufacturing and critical industries our country relies on to remain competitive.

Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.

Maintain adherence to radiation protection, hazardous material handling, and chemical safety protocols.

Current undergraduate or graduate student pursuing a degree in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, or a related field.

Collaborative team member who thrives in fast-paced, multidisciplinary environments and is eager to learn.

As a Mechanical Engineering Intern / Co-op at GITAI, you will join the team developing hardware for our Space-Based Interceptor program. Depending on program needs, you may work on satellite bus components, rocket motor hardware, mechanical interfaces, prototypes, ground support equipment, or test fixtures.
You will take a defined piece of hardware from an early concept into the real world. This may include creating CAD and drawings, working through manufacturing issues with technicians or suppliers, supporting assembly and inspection, preparing and running tests, and updating the design based on the results. The work moves quickly, and you may shift between your desk, the shop floor, suppliers, and test sites.

About Instead
Instead is where tax work gets done. Our AI agent orchestrates the entirety of how work gets done in tax, from preparation and compliance to filing and advisory. It's a fundamentally new way of doing tax work, and it's why top 500 firms, Big Four teams, and enterprise corporate tax departments are choosing Instead.
What makes us unique: we hold full government approvals with the IRS, 48 states, and all cities to e-file 1040, 1041, 1120, 1120S, and 1065, with 706, 709, 990, 5500, 2290, and PPT coming for tax year 2026. Instead is a full replacement for CCH Axcess, GoSystem, UltraTax, OneSource, CorpTax, Lacerte, ProConnect, Drake, and more. No other tax startup will be able to offer these capabilities for years as we are two to three years ahead of everyone else in government approvals. This lets us build product experiences that are simply unmatched in the market.
Instead is backed by Conviction, IRIS (the largest tax software provider in the UK), Skylark, Aprio, and many of our partners and customers. Our team includes leaders from Intuit, Gusto, Zenefits, Thomson Reuters, Wolters Kluwer, PwC, BDO, RSM, and KPMG.
The Role
We're looking for Software Engineering Interns to join our San Francisco team and build real features on our AI-powered tax platform. This is not a coffee-fetching internship. You'll ship production code that hundreds of accounting firms use, work alongside senior engineers, and get hands-on experience building with AI tools from day one.
Our stack: Vue, Nuxt, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS on the frontend. Go, Docker on AWS ECS/Fargate, and PostgreSQL on AWS RDS on the backend. For AI, we use Cursor, Claude Code, Helicone, Gemini, and OpenAI, and we're constantly evaluating new tools.
What You'll Do
Ship product features end to end on our live customer platform alongside senior engineers
Build and test AI-powered components including inference pipelines and prompt engineering
Fix bugs and make product improvements based on real customer feedback
Create internal tools that make the engineering team more productive
Learn our full stack and contribute across frontend, backend, and AI layers
Participate in code reviews, architecture discussions, and product planning
What You Bring
Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field
Strong programming fundamentals. You can write clean code, debug efficiently, and think about edge cases
Familiarity with web development (frontend or backend). Experience with any modern framework counts
Curiosity about AI and willingness to learn. Experience with AI coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) is a plus
High attention to detail and a bias for shipping
Ability to work on-site in San Francisco
What Makes Someone Exceptional
You've built and shipped side projects or open-source contributions that demonstrate your ability to go from idea to working product
You already use AI tools in your coding workflow and understand how they change the way software gets built
You learn fast and don't wait to be told what to do. When you see something broken, you fix it
You care about the end user, not just the code. You want to understand why something matters before you build it
You're excited about working at a startup where your work ships to real customers on day one
Location
San Francisco (on-site)
Instead is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate candidates based on capability, judgment, ownership, and fit for the role's responsibilities. We welcome candidates who can help us build a category-defining company in tax technology.

We’ve built the infrastructure and application that serve as the interface between businesses and consumers. We now have over 167,000 customers, billions of consumer profiles, and hundreds of billions of customer messages and follow-on conversion data. We have a big opportunity to build state-of-the-art AI and machine learning technologies at Klaviyo to power our products and develop AI agents that can automatically create and execute marketing or customer experiences, strategies, and campaigns for any business.
About our Internship
At Klaviyo, our Engineering team builds the foundational technologies that power how brands grow through owned marketing. As an AI Engineering Intern at Klaviyo, you’ll play a key role in designing and building scalable backend systems and user experiences that power our AI products and AI agent solutions. You’ll partner closely with product managers, machine learning engineers, and data scientists, to drive real-world impact at scale. This is a backend-heavy role with opportunities to influence architecture, async processing pipelines, distributed systems, and more.
This internship is an opportunity to apply your generative AI and agentic AI application skills in a production environment. You’ll be embedded within one of our engineering teams and work on meaningful projects that help customers interact with powerful marketing tools, all while building a strong technical foundation and connections across Klaviyo.
Interns come to Klaviyo with experience in a variety of technical skills, but they are all passionate about building, owning and scaling features end-to-end from scratch and breaking through any obstacle or technical challenge in their way. As an AI-first company you will be encouraged to use AI tools to support your work, accelerate learning, and succeed in your role.
How You’ll Make an Impact
Design and build backend systems that support scaling our AI solutions for 200K+ customers.
Develop robust, reliable and scalable services to serve AI models in production environments.
Contribute to evolving our agentic architecture — making our AI agents more self-sufficient and performant.
Contribute to a culture of ownership, experimentation, and customer-centric product thinking.
Engage with internal stakeholders to understand their needs and resolve blockers.
Stay abreast of emerging AI trends and technologies, identifying and leveraging opportunities for their application within Klaviyo’s ecosystem.
Work with the team on project planning and defining achievements, identifying dependencies, and meeting business goals.
What We’re Looking For
Pursuing an advanced degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related field, Graduating in December 2027 or May/June 2028
Previous internship experience in AI, machine learning, or related fields, with a strong interest in building and deploying AI projects.
Have hands-on experience building and deploying generative AI and agentic AI applications into production.
Demonstrate practical experience with key components of agentic architectures, including orchestration, evaluation, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and safety guardrails.
Proficient in Python and modern backend frameworks (FastAPI, Django preferred).
Experience creating human and automated evals to ensure high AI model quality.
Able to thrive in a fast-moving, startup-like environment.
Nice to Have
Trained ML models in the past and deployed them in production systems to generate impact to businesses
Experience in reinforcement learning
Experience with large-scale data processing tools including Spark.
Experience building large scale backend systems

Our Summer Internship Program is an 11-week paid experience [June 1–August 13] at our Boston, MA headquarters. Interns are in office 5 days a week.
Offers will be team agnostic - interns are placed on a team approximately 30 days from the start of the program. Team placement can be on a full-stack, back-end, or front-end team within any of the pillars.

You'll join your team ready to dive into real project work from day one.
Our Boston office is genuinely fun. Lunch is on us 5 days a week, along with free snacks and drinks, ping pong, Nintendo Switch, a golf simulator, and a speakeasy to unwind in.

At Labelbox, we're building the critical infrastructure that powers breakthrough AI models at leading research labs and enterprises. We're the only company offering three integrated solutions for frontier AI development:
Enterprise Platform & Tools: Advanced annotation tools, workflow automation, and quality control systems that enable teams to produce high-quality training data at scale
Frontier Data Labeling Service: Specialized data labeling through Alignerr, leveraging subject matter experts for next-generation AI models
Expert Marketplace: Connecting AI teams with highly skilled annotators and domain experts for flexible scaling
Why Join Us
High-Impact Environment: We operate like an early-stage startup, focusing on impact over process. You'll take on expanded responsibilities quickly, with career growth directly tied to your contributions.
Technical Excellence: Work at the cutting edge of AI development, collaborating with industry leaders and shaping the future of artificial intelligence.
Innovation at Speed: We celebrate those who take ownership, move fast, and deliver impact. Our environment rewards high agency and rapid execution.
Continuous Growth: Every role requires continuous learning and evolution. You'll be surrounded by curious minds solving complex problems at the frontier of AI.
Clear Ownership: You'll know exactly what you're responsible for and have the autonomy to execute. We empower people to drive results through clear ownership and metrics.
Role Overview
As a Security Engineering Intern at Labelbox, you will work closely with our security team to strengthen and scale our enterprise security program. You will receive direct mentorship while gaining hands-on experience across cloud security, application security, SecOps, and compliance workflows. Your work will help improve the security posture of our infrastructure, services, and internal tooling. This is an hourly internship position.
Your Impact
Support day to day triage and analysis of incoming security issues, including operating our Vulnerability Management program.
Contribute to improving access workflows in our identity and access management systems.
Audit and refine access controls for core data platforms and cloud resources.
Assist in strengthening CI/CD security by integrating automated checks that enforce secure development practices early in the lifecycle.
Help operate and optimize our Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platform by tuning alerts, improving log ingestion, and building lightweight automations.
Participate in major internal security initiatives, such as supporting a Cybersecurity Tabletop Exercise and documenting findings.
Research and evaluate enhancements to our security tool stack and contribute to related internal documentation and optimization efforts.
What You Bring
We are looking for a highly motivated and curious individual with a strong interest in the challenges of modern security engineering.
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
A demonstrated interest in cloud security, data security, and security operations.
High degree of ownership, initiative, and willingness to dive into complex technical problems.
Basic understanding of cloud platforms such as GCP, AWS, or Azure, as well as foundational database concepts including SQL or data warehousing.
Demonstrated ability to integrate modern AI tools and local LLM agents (such as Cursor or Claude Code) into your workflow to increase efficiency and solve technical problems faster.
Strong analytical, organizational, and time management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication abilities, including clear documentation of technical findings.
Curiosity, eagerness to learn, and a desire to grow through mentorship across diverse areas of security engineering.
Security Engineering at Labelbox
Our Security Engineering team partners closely with engineering and infrastructure teams to ensure we deliver secure, reliable, and trusted systems for our customers. We focus on building scalable security controls, driving secure development practices, and continually evolving our detection, response, and risk management capabilities. Interns on our team gain exposure to real world security challenges while contributing directly to initiatives that support Labelbox’s growth and security maturity.

About Moment Energy
Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it.
Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone.
The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy.
Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact.
We were told second-life batteries would never be safe enough or scalable enough. We didn’t argue, we engineered the solution. Today, Moment Energy delivers 5x the energy density and holds the certifications required to deploy energy independence at scale.
Now is the moment. Join us.
The Opportunity
We are seeking a Mechanical Engineering Co-op to join our Engineering team, starting in January 2027. In this role, you will support the design, development, and testing of our battery energy storage systems while gaining hands-on experience working alongside experienced engineers.
You will contribute to mechanical design, fabrication, testing, and documentation while helping bring new products from concept through prototype and testing. This is a great opportunity for a student who enjoys hands-on work and wants to apply mechanical engineering principles to real-world clean energy technology.
Responsibilities and Duties
Support the mechanical design and integration of battery energy storage systems
Use 3D CAD software to create models and develop detailed mechanical drawings
Contribute to the research, development, and improvement of mechanical subsystems
Assist with hands-on fabrication and assembly of enclosures and subsystems
Perform basic mechanical and electrical assembly tasks including installing fasteners, connectors, and wiring harnesses
Assist in mechanical and system-level testing and document results
Produce design documentation, test documentation, and FMEA documentation
Support mechanical builds, prototype testing, and troubleshooting during development
Collaborate with engineers to ensure products are reliable, manufacturable, and ready for production
The Student we’re looking for:
Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline
Strong preference for students with design team or previous co-op experience
Strong preference for students available for an 8-month co-op term
Experience with 3D CAD software (SolidWorks, Inventor, or similar)
Career interest in mechanical design, prototyping, and product development
Hands-on experience with fabrication, assembly, or prototyping (school projects, labs, or personal projects are acceptable)
Understanding of mechanical drawings, tolerancing, and engineering documentation
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills
Detail-oriented with good documentation and communication skills
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced engineering environment
The Experience You’ll Gain:
Hands-on experience developing real subsystems used in energy storage systems
Mentorship from experienced professional mechanical engineers
Exposure to product development, prototyping, and testing
The opportunity to contribute to technology supporting the clean energy transition
Why join us?
Today, we’re delivering 5x the energy density and have all the certifications needed to ship energy independence to the world.
Be part of a mission-driven company focused on creating sustainable energy solutions and making a positive impact on the world.
Collaborate closely with passionate co-founders and a team committed to innovation and excellence.
Contribute to building and scaling a company from the ground up, where your work will have a direct and meaningful impact.
Thrive in a workplace that values collaboration, wellness, and celebrating successes, with regular company socials, fitness sessions, and more.
We're a fast-paced and dynamic team.
Every day you'll be taking on a new challenge and learning something new. You'll take on a wide breadth of tasks and contribute to disrupting the battery industry. You'll be part of a tight-knit team that is working together to save the planet! Fun, health, and wellness are incorporated into our daily schedule and we encourage all our team members to bring innovative ideas to the table to create an interactive workplace.
Moment Energy Benefits Highlights (full time, permanent employees only)
Financial Growth: Employee equity and a robust RRSP matching program.
Comprehensive Health Coverage: Extended health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents through Manulife.
Generous Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off plus a paid company closure between Christmas and New Year's, with a generous paid sick leave.
Vibrant Culture & Perks: Open and collaborative office culture, frequent company socials and wellness programs (weekly yoga/fitness), and free EV charging on-site.
Company Dinner: Weekly Tuesday dinner provided by Moment Energy. We also have a generous supply of coffee and snacks for the office!
Our Commitments
Moment Energy is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to inclusive, barrier-free recruitment and selection processes, including our work environment. We especially welcome applications from Indigenous peoples, members of racialized communities, persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+.
—---
Our Values
Our values are key to how we show up every day at Moment Energy! We keep them in the forefront of what we do, and they’re used everywhere. We refer to them when we have tough decisions to make, we give shoutouts based on living out these values, and we include them as part of our performance reviews.
We have 5 core values and 1 foundational pillar (Safety is our Foundation) which lays the groundwork for everything we do.
Safety is our Foundation
We prioritize the safety of our products, customers, employees, and the general public above all else. From the workshop to the field, we maintain the highest standards for our batteries in testing manufacturing and deployment, and daily operations. Safety is not only about procedures—it is about vigilance, responsibility, and speaking up when something does not feel right.
Safety is everyone's responsibility. We follow safety protocols, use proper equipment, and continuously improve our systems to prevent risks before they occur. If something is unsafe, we stop work and address it.
Safety also means protecting our colleagues, customers, and communities by designing reliable products, maintaining safe workspaces, and ensuring our work is done carefully and responsibly.
We’re Building a Greener Future Together:
We infuse passion for our cleantech mission into every aspect of our work and incorporate fun into the workplace. We motivate one another, celebrate our successes and embrace eco-friendly practices to reduce our carbon footprint.
We Prioritize our Customer’s Needs:
We place our customers at the core of everything we do, ensuring that every decision considers their needs and aims to provide increased value to them. We provide reliable support for our customers, every step of the way.
We’re Open, Honest and Accountable:
We prioritize open and honest communication to foster mutual understanding, strengthen knowledge sharing, and reduce miscommunication within the team. We admit when we’ve made a mistake, and remedy our actions. We transparently communicate outcomes whether good, bad, or unexpected.
We Think and Act like Owners:
We’re self-starters that proactively embrace new challenges along with personal and collective ownership of responsibilities in the organization. We focus on growth, not titles, and we do what needs to be done.
We Treat Everyone with Respect:
We actively listen, share openly, and work together towards common goals. We treat one another with mutual respect to cultivate an inclusive environment where everyone feels accepted, supported, and heard. We keep an open mind and are willing to learn.

Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it.
Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone.
The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy.

Collaborate with engineering teams to integrate data-driven insights into product development and system optimization

As a Quality Control Intern you will play a key role in supporting the design, development, and manufacturing processes of our spacecraft components. Inspection and Testing: Assist in the inspection and testing of spacecraft components and systems to ensure they meet stringent quality and performance standards.

Process Improvement: Analyze manufacturing and assembly processes to identify areas where quality can be improved and help implement corrective actions.

Educational Background: Currently pursuing a degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Physics, or a related field.
Technical Skills:
Knowledge of basic manufacturing and assembly processes used in aerospace engineering.
Familiarity with quality control tools and techniques, including inspection methods, statistical process control (SPC), and root cause analysis.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) for data management and reporting.
Basic understanding of CAD software or other design tools is a plus.
Attention to Detail: Strong attention to detail and ability to identify small discrepancies that could have a significant impact on spacecraft performance and safety.
Analytical Skills: Ability to analyze test data, identify trends, and propose and make improvements to processes or products.
Communication Skills: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document findings clearly and present them to team members and stakeholders.
Problem-Solving Mindset: Ability to approach problems analytically, contributing to continuous improvement efforts within the quality control process.
Passion for Space: A strong interest in space exploration and aerospace technologies, with a commitment to ensuring the highest quality in spacecraft systems.
Nice-to-have Skills
Familiarity with aerospace industry standards such as AS9100, ISO 9001, or similar.
Experience in a lab or manufacturing environment related to aerospace or engineering.
Experience with quality management software or tools like Minitab, Qlik, or other data analysis platforms.
Understanding of environmental and reliability testing for spacecraft components.

PhD $50/hour

Summer internships will range between the months of May and September depending on university schedules. Internship is full-time and on-site in San Jose, California.
The Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) team at Muon is responsible for validating spacecraft hardware through unit acceptance testing as well as spacecraft-level integration and environmental testing. As an Environmental Test Engineering Intern, you will support the planning, setup, execution, and analysis of environmental tests used to validate spacecraft hardware against the extreme conditions of launch and space.
You will work alongside experienced environmental test engineers, test engineers, and technicians to prepare hardware and test equipment, develop and execute test procedures, collect and analyze test data, and troubleshoot test issues. This is a hands-on opportunity to gain experience with spacecraft environmental testing and see your work directly contribute to the successful integration and launch of Muon spacecraft.
Muon is a small and fast growing startup which offers interns the experience to get direct mentorship and have real impact on our programs. As an intern, you'll collaborate with a dynamic team in a startup environment and have the chance to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the industry. We're committed to offering an experience where your decisions and contributions play a pivotal role in driving Muon's success.
Responsibilities
Assist environmental test engineers with the planning, preparation, and execution of spacecraft and subsystem environmental testing, including thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, and other qualification or acceptance testing.
Support test setup and instrumentation, including thermocouples, accelerometers, pressure sensors, and other test measurement equipment.
Assist with preparing spacecraft hardware, fixtures, ground support equipment, and test configurations for environmental test campaigns.
Execute functional checkouts and test procedures under engineer supervision before, during, and after environmental testing.
Monitor test operations and hardware performance, identify anomalies, and support troubleshooting and root-cause investigations.
Collect, process, and perform preliminary analysis of environmental test data to verify hardware performance and test requirements.
Support development and improvement of test procedures, test processes, checklists, and laboratory workflows.
Assist with configuration and operation of environmental test equipment and data acquisition systems.
Support automation and scripting efforts to improve environmental test setup, monitoring, data collection, and analysis.
Generate test documentation, data summaries, and reports under the guidance of environmental test engineers.
Support integration and handling of spacecraft hardware and ground support equipment in cleanroom, laboratory, and environmental test facilities.
Help maintain a safe, organized, and flight-hardware-ready test environment.
Qualifications
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field.
Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals, particularly in areas such as mechanics, thermal systems, dynamics, instrumentation, or electrical systems.
Demonstrated interest in spacecraft environmental testing, laboratory testing, or hardware development.
Experience with a programming or scripting language for data analysis or test automation, such as Python, MATLAB/Simulink, Julia, or C++.
Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to approach complex technical challenges from a first-principles perspective.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with an ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment.
Ability and willingness to work hands-on with engineering hardware and test equipment.
Nice-to-have Skills
Previous internship, co-op, research, or laboratory experience involving hardware testing.
Experience with thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, shock, or other environmental testing.
Experience with data acquisition systems, instrumentation, sensors, or test equipment.
Experience developing test procedures, test plans, or test reports.
Experience with accelerometers, thermocouples, pressure transducers, strain gauges, or similar instrumentation.
Experience with Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or other tools used for test automation and data analysis.
Previous experience on technical project teams such as a CubeSat, rocketry, Formula SAE, Solar Car, or other hardware-focused engineering project.
Familiarity with spacecraft systems or subsystems and environmental test requirements.
Experience with hardware integration, troubleshooting, or hardware-in-the-loop testing.

Location: New York, fully in-office (no remote work)
Dates: 14th June 2027 – 22nd August 2027
Join Marshall Wace for the summer and experience first-hand what it means to be a member of the highly innovative and fast-paced technology team that powers one of the world's largest hedge funds. Interns in this programme will be given projects that both provide real-world engineering experience and drive our business forward. Technology touches every aspect of MW, and interns will have the opportunity to build systems that enable success in domains throughout the business. These domains include our systematic and fundamental investment strategies, firmwide technology platform, trading and order execution, AI-powered automation and enhancements of workflows, and many others.
Prior to the start of the internship, our various tech teams will propose potential projects for interns. We select the projects that are the most valuable to the firm and that stand to provide the most engaging and valuable experience. Interns are then assigned to selected projects in pairs, reporting to a senior engineer. Throughout the internship, interns receive comprehensive support from our teams. In addition to direct mentorship by their managers, this support includes regular seminars on the many segments of the MW tech estate, informational sessions on other areas of the business with senior leaders, social events, and opportunities to engage in the firm’s charitable activities. All of this is in service of our goal to provide our interns with extensive professional and technical development and a broad understanding of our business and of the finance industry at large.
Examples of past projects:
A backtesting framework for our quantitative trading system
Horizontally distributed autonomous coding agents
AI-driven user behaviour analytics platform
What are we looking for?
This internship is ideal for an innovative problem solver who can demonstrate inventive and creative use of technology. Successful participants may have the opportunity to return full time as a member of our Technology Graduate Programme when they complete their studies.
We don’t specifically look for those working towards a computer science degree, but we do look for those who are high-achieving academically and have actively developed technical, software engineering skills. This could be through coursework, previous internships, research, or even just the pursuit of a passion for technology in their free time.
Finally, we also believe that the right person is more than just a technical expert. We place real value on collaboration, entrepreneurialism, and strong communication skills. The structure of the technology organisation here is such that every engineer must own their work end to end. That means successful interns, and full-time team members, will play an active role in identifying opportunities for impact through technology, designing the solution to capture that potential, building it, and working directly with stakeholders throughout the firm to align engineering efforts with value creation.
Why join us?
Technology is at our core. It’s industry-defining and best-in-class, but we are striving for even more. You’ll have the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technologies while learning from some of the best technicians in the business. As a technology intern, this is a chance to accelerate your skill set and gain invaluable real-world experience.
Progression at Marshall Wace
The aim of our internships is to convert the best performers into graduates. The rotational format of our graduate program then allows you to explore various roles within the Technology team before determining the best fit for you. Upon completing your rotations, you have the flexibility to advance to the team that aligns most with your interests and strengths.
After completing the program, the progression paths are not rigidly defined. There is no predetermined ladder for you to climb. Instead, your personal growth may involve taking on more challenging projects, mentoring a team or new hires, or even pursuing opportunities for international assignments. Your individual development path is open for exploration, and you can collaborate with your management to shape what your future growth looks like.
Marshall Wace is an equal opportunity employer. Individuals seeking employment are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other category protected by applicable law.
Note: we request that you only apply to the one role you are most interested in. This includes both the position itself and the location. Duplicate applications will cause delays in processing your application.
In accordance with New York State and New York City pay transparency laws, the annual base salary for this position is $150,000 (pro rata for the internship period). Actual compensation may vary based on factors such as experience, qualifications, and location. This role may also be eligible for a discretionary bonus and benefits.

Nanopath is developing a first-in-class in vitro diagnostics platform to transform how diseases are diagnosed. We aim to replace lengthy molecular testing workflows by bringing rapid, high-quality diagnostics closer to the patient. Support and manage a variety of assay development tasks. We are happy to tailor key responsibilities to the candidate ranging from molecular biology, cell culture, biomanufacturing, and bioinformatics.
Participate in critical team discussions, meetings, and presentations. Our co-ops are given critical and important projects!
Work directly with our tight-knit team of scientists and engineers to drive our product forward.
Learn more about cutting edge biophysics and interdisciplinary medtech development.

Ability to commit to 15+ weeks of full-time and onsite work in Cambridge, MA
Current enrollment in a relevant academic program – we are open to undergraduate and graduate degree opportunities
Sophomore or above with demonstrated experience through past internships or research projects

Proactive self-starter with eagerness to adapt to a fast-paced, dynamic startup environment
Passion for technology translation and willingness to shape Nanopath’s future

We are creating devices that enable a bi-directional interface with the brain. These devices allow us to restore movement to the paralyzed, restore sight to the blind, and revolutionize how humans interact with their digital world.
Team Description:
The Robot Software Team builds software that enables scalable neurosurgery that allows safe implantation of the N1 device, ranging from core control, sensors and perception, autonomy, surgery analytics, and more. This role tightly integrates with the robot hardware team, surgery engineering team, as well as the BCI applications team which rely on us to deliver safe and effective implantation of the N1 device.
Neuralink strives to be a meritocratic environment: we require honest and transparent communication to ensure the best ideas win out, and we believe the best solutions emerge and the best teams are created when you assemble high-performing individuals and allow them to engage in rigorous and thoughtful inquiry. We want to work with exceptional people, and, to the extent that you excel, we want you to take on more responsibility and help all of us succeed. If this speaks to you, come join us.
Job Description and Responsibilities:
As a Software Engineer Intern on the Robot Software Team, you will be responsible for writing software and making sure your code works on an actual surgical robot, not just simulation. Our robotics integrate actuated devices with microelectromechanical systems as well as novel surgical procedures. These applications place strong emphasis on high-precision, high-repeatability mechanical motion, as well as high reliability and fail-safe design. You will be expected to:
Develop safety-critical software for the robot; you are responsible for contributing directly to surgery-ready software as an intern
Take ownership of a project that is integral to robot functioning from design to implementation under the guidance of a robot software team member
Jump on problems when they arise with a strong bias for action to support robot operation by non-software teams
Work across different engineering disciplines; your software may involve interactions with the mechanical, electrical, biological, and neuroscience teams
Required Qualifications:
Evidence of exceptional ability in engineering or computer science
Experience in writing performant applications in a system language like C, C++, and Rust
Ability to work on mission-critical and safety-critical systems
Strong bias for action and first principles thinking
Preferred Qualifications:
Hands-on experience with robotics or high-reliability systems
Experience coding in Linux and debugging on Linux systems
Experience in computer vision
Experience in kinematics and motion planning
Experience working on medical robots
Experience working in a high-precision environment

Perpay is a certified B Corp and Philadelphia’s most impactful growth-stage startup. We are driven by a mission to significantly improve the financial stability of everyday Americans. For the past decade, we have established strong product-market fit and a profitable, efficient operating model across a suite of products, positioning Perpay as the premier financial partner for consumers with subprime credit.
With over 500,000 customers who have utilized more than $1 billion in spending power, we are at a pivotal moment. We are scaling our operations, building new offerings, and deepening our impact. We are looking for teammates eager to join us on this journey.
Our venture partners include First Round Capital and L Catterton.
Products we’ve built to make an impact:
Perpay Marketplace: Combines interest-free payments and modern e-commerce to reduce cost of ownership and promote healthy repayment behavior.
Perpay+: Leverages Marketplace repayment history to help members monitor and build credit with all 3 credit bureaus.
Perpay Credit Card: Expands access to the flexibility and benefits of a World Mastercard by removing common barriers like high security deposits and low approval odds.
Our team thrives on in-person collaboration, operating from our unique center-city Philadelphia office. This comfortable "home away from home" space offers river views and fosters rapid product development, strong relationships, and career growth. The energy from achieving big wins is palpable here. While we primarily work in the office, we offer sensible flexibility for personal needs, such as sick children or urgent errands, and coordinate official remote weeks around major holidays. If you are passionate about a meaningful mission, collaboration, equity, and generous perks, Perpay is the best place to be in Philadelphia right now.
About the Role:
As a business operations intern at Perpay, your main responsibility is to learn! We understand the value of mentorship and offer students an opportunity to gain real work experience before graduation. In the 10-12 weeks we'll be together, you will be expected to support our Business Operations team and their daily responsibilities. You’ll gain exposure to all operational functions including: Approvals & Account Management, E-Commerce Operations, Payments & Reconciliation, and Customer Success. In addition to working on projects of real impact, you will have the ability to meet with various business owners to drive personal and professional development and expand your network. All while developing the skills to succeed in a fast-paced tech start-up environment and experiencing and contributing to our unique culture.
Our greatest strength is our people and we’d love for you to be one of them!
What You'll Bring:
Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s program, with the expected graduation date between winter 2027 – summer 2028 (or equivalent experience)
Cumulative GPA of 3.0 or better
Excellent verbal & written communication skills
Interest in Business Operations, Marketing, Accounting & Finance, or Product Development.
Drive: someone who has the desire to continuously grow and develop
Attention to detail: you are organized, attentive, and focused
Positivity: you are optimistic, collaborative, and confident
Resiliency: you embrace and thrive on change, easily adapting to shifting priorities
Hey, we know not everybody checks all the boxes, so if you’re interested, please apply because you could be just what we’re looking for!

ABOUT PROPRIETARY RESEARCH
On our proprietary research team—Market Intelligence—you’ll partner with our Investment Professionals and Compliance team to uncover insights about companies, industries, and the broader economy through deep fundamental research.
Canvas is the supply chain research group within Market Intelligence. Canvas conducts compliant supply chain research by developing deep industry expertise, talking with private company executives, and synthesizing information for portfolio managers and analysts. Our team produces impactful research that will change the way you look at the world.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
This 6-month intensive fellowship offers hands-on experience in research, business analysis, cross-functional collaboration, and the investment process within a fast-paced, compliance-focused environment. Canvas Fellows will be considered for permanent placement on the team following completion of the program.
When you join the Canvas team, you’re signing up for the learning experience of a lifetime. You will never look at anything the same way—from grocery stores to tires to semiconductors. Every day, Canvas team members speak with private company executives and learn about the businesses they’ve spent their lives building. The team synthesizes findings in comprehensive reports that are consumed by Point72 investment professionals.
Other Market Intelligence divisions do quantitative research to explain what is going on in an industry. As a Fundamental Researcher, your qualitative research will explain the why. During the 6-month program based in our New York office, you will:
Become a subject matter expert on an assigned industry
Engage with small, medium, and large private company executives about their businesses and the industries in which they operate, gathering qualitative data on key development—including structural shifts, real-time changes in supply/demand dynamics, and emerging competitors, markets, and technologies—with a focus on understanding why they are happening
Synthesize your findings in comprehensive reports that present a view of the industry
Gain unparalleled exposure to, and learn from, business leaders across industries, including private company executives and your colleagues
Interact directly with our investment professionals and learn the discretionary investment process to help drive more informed investment decisions
Partner on the above with dedicated Compliance professionals
WHAT EXCITES YOU
Staying current on the evolving alternative data market and its role in discretionary investing
Speaking with experts both inside and outside the firm to understand data needs and offerings
Analytical thinking and sifting through available data to find “the answer”
Fast-paced work environments that at times require switching gears to address the needs of the business
Working as part of a cross-functional team comprising investment, research, and compliance professionals
WHAT EXCITES US
Excellent attention to detail, organization, and project management skills
Superb business intuition and a solution orientated, methodical approach to problem-solving
Ability to collaborate and build relationships across multiple business units within the firm
People who “elevate the room” through their work ethic, curiosity, and solution-orientated attitude
Commitment to the highest ethical standards
WHAT’S REQUIRED
Undergraduate degree conferred in 2025 or 2026
Strong analytical skills
Excellent written and verbal communication abilities
An eagerness to find out if your conclusions are right or wrong
An understanding of how companies work (their processes and outcomes) or an interest in learning
Intellectual curiosity, creative thinking, maturity
Highest standards of ethical decision making
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
