After successful completion of a CLDP Summer internship at Alcon, interns may be considered for participation in the Commercial Leadership Development Program full-time. Commercial Leadership Development Program (CLDP) at Alcon is a key pipeline for graduate degree talent with ambition to advance into leadership positions within Alcon Commercial functions. Exceptional individuals chosen for this highly selective and challenging program engage in tailored rotational experiences towards a leadership career path. Members will engage in three, year-long rotations. Rotations will include a Commercial Foundation rotation (Commercial Operations), a Marketing rotation, and a Sales rotation. Program benefits will include Mentor Program, Functional Programming, Networking Events, Tailored Development, and Executive Presentations on key learnings and outcomes of rotations.

Summer Intern – Firmware Engineer, Allegion Access Technologies – Farmington, Connecticut
As an Allegion Firmware Engineer intern, you will contribute meaningful work and make a direct impact to the Firmware/Embedded Software competency. You will gain hands-on experience defining and implementing firmware features for access control and automatic door systems, support product validation, and collaborate closely with hardware, test, and manufacturing teams. If you are seeking a summer experience that offers meaningful work, learning opportunities, professional development, and an opportunity to build strong relationships with your peers and leaders, Allegion is the right place for you!
What You Will Do:
Develop, debug, and test embedded firmware for microcontroller-based products.
Participate in requirements definition and design discussions for new firmware features and product updates.
Implement and maintain device drivers, communication stacks (UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, Ethernet, BLE as applicable), and peripheral interfacing.
Work with real-time operating systems (RTOS) and bare-metal architectures as required by product designs.
Support hardware bring-up and verification by using tools such as debuggers (JTAG/SWD), logic analyzers, and oscilloscopes.
Design tools to measure and analyze existing and new products.
Participate in code reviews, version control workflows, and continuous integration/build processes.
Document firmware design, test procedures, release notes, and standard operating procedures.
Utilize tools such as functional block diagrams, flow diagrams, state-diagrams, and others as required in product development.
Work with a team to create well-rounded solutions.
Deepen your understanding of basic electronics and the use of electrical tools, such as a digital multi-meter, oscilloscope, and digital logic analyzers.
Obtain the experience to create a foundation for growth and future opportunities with Allegion
What You Need to Succeed:
Pursuing a degree in a relevant discipline, e.g., Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering Technology, and Electrical Engineering Technology.
Demonstrated leadership ability and initiative, e.g., school club officer, sports team captain, resident advisor, leadership on school or work projects, etc.
Preferred knowledge of C programming language.
Preferred knowledge of working with embedded microprocessors and their associated IDE and tools.
Basic electronics understanding, including low voltage wiring.
Passion to be hands-on and able to work in an engineering laboratory environment.
Ability to work in both a team and individual setting.
Resiliency and ability to adapt quickly.
Effective listening, time management and creative problem-solving techniques.
A desire to learn, grow and develop by working on projects that will impact Allegion’s business and customers.

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.
Job Description
We are seeking students for our Summer 2027 Internship Program. The Quantum Algorithm Development Intern will support research and development efforts focused on applying quantum computing to real-world optimization, machine learning, and analytics challenges. Working alongside technical experts, interns will develop and evaluate quantum algorithms, build simulations and prototypes, analyze quantum and classical approaches, and contribute to collaborative projects with industry and academic partners. This role is ideal for senior undergraduate students, graduate students, or recent graduates with a background in computer science, physics, mathematics, engineering, or a related field who are passionate about emerging technologies, problem-solving, and translating advanced research into practical applications.
This position is part of our Summer 2027 Internship Program.
This internship is designed for senior-level undergraduate students, graduate students, and recent graduates interested in applying quantum computing to real-world optimization, machine learning, and analytics challenges. Preference will be given to candidates in the Chicago, IL area.
As a Quantum Algorithm Development Intern, you will work alongside technical experts to explore emerging quantum technologies, contribute to projects collaborating with partners in industry and academia, and investigate how quantum and classical approaches can be applied to complex business problems.
The ideal candidate is intellectually curious, enjoys solving difficult problems, and has a strong foundation in computing, mathematics, analytics, or engineering. This role offers hands-on experience conducting research, developing technical solutions, and communicating findings in a rapidly evolving field.
Key Responsibilities
As an intern, you will:
Assist in the development and evaluation of quantum computing algorithms for optimization, machine learning, and related applications.
Build simulations and prototypes using quantum and classical computing tools.
Analyze and compare the performance of quantum and classical approaches through numerical experiments.
Investigate a defined technical or research question with guidance from members of the team.
Contribute to research studies, technical documentation, presentations, and proof-of-concept projects.
Collaborate with internal teams and, when applicable, external researchers from universities, national laboratories, and industry.
Help identify practical problems that could potentially benefit from future advances in quantum computing.
Learn and apply best practices in scientific computing, data analysis, and algorithm development.
Communicate progress, raise questions when support is needed, and incorporate feedback throughout the project.
Minimum Qualifications
Current undergraduate student entering senior year, current graduate student, or recent graduate pursuing a degree in:
Computer Science
Physics
Mathematics
Statistics
Data Science
Industrial Engineering
Operations Research
Electrical Engineering
Or a related quantitative or technical field
Coursework, research, or project experience in one or more of the following areas:
Quantum Computing
Linear Algebra
Algorithms
Mathematical Optimization
Machine Learning
Scientific Computing
Experience programming in Python or a similar technical programming language.
Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly.
Demonstrated curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn by asking questions and tackling unfamiliar challenges.
Interest in emerging technologies and their real-world applications.
Preferred Qualifications
Strong candidates bring experience from a Quantum Computing track, in combination with a Classical Analytics track, or related fields. While some prior exposure to quantum computing is required, applicants are not expected to have experience in every area listed below.
Quantum Computing Background
One or more of the following:
Introductory coursework or project experience in quantum computing.
Familiarity with quantum circuits or quantum algorithms.
Experience with quantum software frameworks such as Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane, CUDA-Q, or similar tools.
Coursework, research, or projects involving quantum information science.
Classical Analytics Background
One or more of the following:
Machine learning or predictive modeling.
Mathematical optimization, operations research, or decision science.
Data analysis, statistics, or scientific computing.
Experience with optimization libraries, machine learning frameworks, or numerical methods.
Experience applying analytical or computational methods to technical or business problems.
What Will Help You Succeed
Successful interns in this role will demonstrate:
Intellectual curiosity and an interest in investigating unanswered questions.
Ability to work independently while communicating when support is needed.
Comfort learning unfamiliar technical concepts.
Ability to explain complex work clearly and concisely.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Openness to feedback and collaboration.
Ability to connect technical findings to practical applications.
Compensation range for this role is between $32.69 and $36.54 an hour depending on experience and qualifications.
Skills
Algorithms, Machine Learning (ML), Physics, Python (Programming Language), Qiskit, Quantum Computing, Technical Research, Written Communication

Architecture interns study hardware and software trade-offs present in the latest version of our chips and explore uses of both to solve real-world problems. Interns may develop software models of important behaviors in hardware co-processors such as memory bandwidth and pipeline latency or develop visualization tools to illustrate architecture behavior. Interns produce support tools to enable software to make efficient use of hardware co-processors. A final presentation at the end of the internships describes their findings and allows other team members to use their work for ongoing projects.
The internship program requires experience in modern programming languages and computer architecture. C++, C, Python, and CUDA are our popular tools. Exposure to common neural networks frameworks such as PyTorch helps. We expect that interns will be able to pick up missing skills quickly, deliver their assignments on time, and present their work at the end of the program.

AI Vision Processors For Edge Applications
Our solutions make cameras smarter by extracting valuable data from high-resolution video streams.

Join us—Where your Career is a Force for Good!

Joining the American Red Cross is like nothing else – it’s as much something you feel as something you do. You become a vital part of the world’s largest humanitarian network. Joining a team of welcoming individuals who are exceptional, yet unassuming. Diverse, yet uncompromising in unity. You grow your career within a movement that matters, where success is measured in people helped, communities made whole, and individuals equipped to never stop changing lives and situations for the better.

Internship opportunity for an undergraduate or graduate student or trainee to gain work experience offered by an organization for a limited period of time. Conduct research related to communication materials. Assist with the creation and maintenance of communications plans, and strategies. Perform all duties and responsibilities in compliance with standard operating procedures and other applicable Federal, State and local regulations.

Note that American Red Cross salaries are aligned to the specific geographic location in which the work is primarily performed. May support Communications team with research projects.
Typically analyze data, present facts, and recommend solutions.
Develop press materials and social media content (posts, reels, videos).
Conduct interviews with volunteers, staff, public for story development.
Attend events in person as needed.
May create, develop, or maintain databases for various lines of service events or projects.
Assist with the development of reports and other informational materials presented to management.
Conduct unit-specific responsibilities.
Scope: Learning aspects of the job. Assignments are received in task- oriented terms. Contacts primarily within immediate work unit.

Education: High School or equivalent required. Internship is typically part of an undergraduate program which requires some university credit hours.
Experience: Up to 1 year of related experience.
Management Experience: N/A
Skills & Abilities: Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Proficient computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, and Excel). Ability to work on a team.
Travel: N/A

Bilingual in Spanish is a plus.
Knowledge of AP Writing Style, social media, video creation and editing.
Great communications skills.
Comfortable with interviewing a variety of audience.
Ability to cultivate and maintain relationships with stakeholders.
Studying Public Relations or Communications.

Ability to use a personal computer, applicable software, and office equipment for sustained periods of time. May include sitting for long periods of time, driving a vehicle, and working under challenging conditions.

As a summer intern, you will join a U.S. Value & Access team and take ownership of a project tied directly to a current business priority. Upon successful completion of the summer experience, interns will be evaluated for a full-time position post-graduation.
This role interacts cross functionally with Value Marketing, Patient Access, Ecosystems & Insights, Sales, Brand Marketing, Government Affairs, Trade & Distribution, Business Unit Leadership, Finance, Accounting, and Legal. This role will provide a strong foundation in the U.S. healthcare landscape while building skills and experience that translate across a range of commercial healthcare careers.

Network with colleagues across the company, including full access to Amgen’s Employee Resource Groups and an on-site visit to Amgen’s headquarters in Thousand Oaks

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. This internship will be approximately 13 weeks that includes both project- based and experiential learning. In conjunction with the project work, you will have the opportunity for professional development through training sessions, one-on-one support, and various networking events.
Be part of Amgen's newest and most advanced drug substance manufacturing plant. When completed, the Amgen North Carolina FleX Batch facility will combine the latest in single-use technologies with traditional stainless-steel equipment to allow for maximum flexibility in operations. Undergrad Intern - Operations – Process Development (Summer 2027)
What You Will Do
Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. Operations is one of the three foundational functions at Amgen with a mission to be consistent and efficient in delivering safe and effective medicines around the world. Operations manufactures and delivers Amgen therapeutics to our patients. Made up of five subfunctions: Global Supply Chain, Process Development, Quality, Manufacturing, and Engineering, and spread across several sites, Operations’ aspiration is simple: Ensure patients have access to the Amgen products they need. Every patient, every time.
Process development (PD) is the department within Operations that takes molecules from Research & Development and turns them into products which can be manufactured for therapeutic use. With the support of their hiring manager, the PD intern will complete a lab-based project in one of the following areas: Drug Substance Technologies, Attribute Sciences, Manufacturing and Clinical Supply, Digital Strategy & Capabilities, Drug Product Technologies, or Combination Product Operations. The intern will be responsible for rigorously conducting and documenting their experiments as well as analyzing and interpreting data into meaningful, business-influencing outcomes, and then communicating this process to their team in a clear and compelling manner.
In conjunction with the project work, interns will have the opportunity for professional development through training sessions, an executive speaker series, lab and facilities tours, one-on-one mentoring, and various networking events. Interns will also be able to interact with peers at Amgen-sponsored social events.
Example projects from previous internships:
Drug Substance Technology – Development of Single-Pass Tangential Flow UF/DF Unit Operation for Production of Ultra-High Concentration Drug Substance
Attribute Sciences – Advancement of Activity Assays for Key Residual Host Cell Proteins
Drug Product Technology – Using Mass Spectrometry as an In-line Process Analytical Tool for Lyophilization
Combination Product Operations – Gathering Patient and Internal Stakeholder Insights to Improve Combination Products and Processes
Manufacturing and Clinical Supply – Tactical Project Management Standardization for Commercial Drug Product Tech Transfers
